Generate an index of chunk offsets and sizes for iterating an MDArray

Source: R/gdal_mdim.R
mdim_chunk_index.Rd

mdim_chunk_index() returns a matrix of chunk indexes, start offsets and sizes for iterating I/O operations over an array of a GDAL Multidimensional Raster dataset, one row per chunk. It is the multidimensional counterpart of make_chunk_index(). This function is experimental. Its interface may change in future releases.

Usage

mdim_chunk_index(x, chunk_size = NULL, start = NULL, count = NULL)

Arguments

x

Either an object of class GDALMDArray, or a numeric vector of dimension sizes (in the array's own dimension order).

chunk_size

Optional numeric vector with the chunk size along each dimension. A value of 0 or NA means the whole dimension. By default, the block size of the array if x is a GDALMDArray object. Required if x is a vector of dimension sizes.

start

Optional numeric vector of 0-based start indexes of a hyperslab, one value per dimension.

count

Optional numeric vector giving the number of values of a hyperslab along each dimension. Required if start is given.

Value

A numeric matrix with one row per chunk and, for an array of n dimensions, 3 * n named columns: chunkoff0, ..., off0, ..., size0, ..., where the suffix is the 0-based dimension index. chunkoff is the 0-based index of the chunk along the dimension, off is its 0-based start index and size is its size. Columns off and size of a row are the start and count arguments for GDALMDArray$read(). Rows are ordered with the last dimension varying fastest.

Details

The chunks tile the array exactly, on a regular grid of chunk_size starting at index 0 of each dimension. Chunks at the end of a dimension are clipped to the array. By default, the chunks are the blocks of the array as stored (see $getBlockSize() of class GDALMDArray), so that each row is a read of exactly one stored block: one fetch and one decode, the natural unit of cost for chunked formats such as Zarr, netCDF-4 and HDF5. A chunk_size from $getProcessingChunkSize() gives larger chunks, aligned to the blocks, that fit a memory limit.

If start and count are given, only the chunks that intersect that hyperslab are returned (as whole chunks, i.e., not clipped to the hyperslab). This gives the stored blocks that a planned read would touch.

See also

GDALMDArray, make_chunk_index(), mdim_read()

Examples

# dimension sizes and chunk sizes given directly
mdim_chunk_index(c(4, 5, 6), c(2, 5, 4))
#>      chunkoff0 chunkoff1 chunkoff2 off0 off1 off2 size0 size1 size2
#> [1,]         0         0         0    0    0    0     2     5     4
#> [2,]         0         0         1    0    0    4     2     5     2
#> [3,]         1         0         0    2    0    0     2     5     4
#> [4,]         1         0         1    2    0    4     2     5     2

# the chunks that a hyperslab read would touch
mdim_chunk_index(c(4, 5, 6), c(2, 5, 4), start = c(1, 0, 3),
                 count = c(1, 5, 1))
#>      chunkoff0 chunkoff1 chunkoff2 off0 off1 off2 size0 size1 size2
#> [1,]         0         0         0    0    0    0     2     5     4

# iterate over an array in chunks that fit a memory limit (here 120 bytes,
# i.e., 60 values of Int16)
f <- system.file("extdata/mdim_small.nc", package="gdalraster")
ds <- new(GDALMultiDimRaster, f)
arr <- ds$openMDArray("/t2m")
idx <- mdim_chunk_index(arr, arr$getProcessingChunkSize(120))
idx
#>      chunkoff0 chunkoff1 chunkoff2 off0 off1 off2 size0 size1 size2
#> [1,]         0         0         0    0    0    0     2     5     6
#> [2,]         1         0         0    2    0    0     2     5     6

off_cols <- startsWith(colnames(idx), "off")
size_cols <- startsWith(colnames(idx), "size")
chunk_max <- numeric(nrow(idx))
for (i in seq_len(nrow(idx))) {
  v <- arr$read(idx[i, off_cols], idx[i, size_cols], NULL)
  chunk_max[i] <- max(v, na.rm = TRUE)
}
chunk_max
#> [1] 1685 1885

arr$close()
ds$close()
